BankableStatus.description: Whether a result is fit for a lender's review.
BankableStatus.title: BankableStatus

CalculationPeriod.description: The period the covenant DSCR is tested over.
CalculationPeriod.title: CalculationPeriod

CapacityAgreementIndexation.description:
The facts para 3(5) needs to index a T-4 payment from year 1 (D129).

``cpi_base`` is the average monthly CPI over the auction's base period (reg 2, reg 11(1)(f));
``cpi_x_year1`` the average over the winter ending 30 April before the first delivery year.
Both are ONS CPI (All Items) index values, stated by the user with a source: both or neither.
Without them the year-1 uplift is 1.0 and labelled as such, never invented.

reference.description: The agreement / register entry / ONS series.
reference.title: Reference

CapacityAgreementIndexation.title: CapacityAgreementIndexation

CapitalRecoveryAccount.description:
The **always-defined** return account (D47/D50, Olly 2026-08-17).

``irr`` and ``equity_irr`` on :class:`FinancialCase` are legitimately nullable: an IRR does not
exist for a series whose every cashflow is non-positive, and guessing one would be worse than
refusing it. But a record whose ONLY return field is that null tells a reader "no value was
found" when the truth is "the value was measured and it falls £N short of returning capital".
This account is therefore **mandatory** on every ``FinancialCase`` and every field but
``capital_recovery_pct`` is non-nullable, so the two statements can never be confused.

Undiscounted by design: the library carries no sourced project discount rate, and discounting at
``financing.target_equity_irr_pct`` (an equity *target*, withdrawn as a hurdle by CLAUDE.md §2)
would be an invented input under D45. Computed by ``gridq.finance.returns.capital_recovery``;
this schema only carries the shape, per the module docstring above.

annual_net_margin_gbp.description: Mean operating-year net cashflow. Negative means the asset loses money yearly.
annual_net_margin_gbp.title: Annual Net Margin Gbp

capital_outlay_gbp.description: Year-0 outlay as a positive number; 0.0 when year 0 is not an outlay.
capital_outlay_gbp.title: Capital Outlay Gbp

capital_recovery_gap_gbp.description: Outlay minus operating cashflow. POSITIVE is a shortfall and is the figure that replaces a null IRR; negative means capital is returned with that much to spare.
capital_recovery_gap_gbp.title: Capital Recovery Gap Gbp

capital_recovery_pct.description: Operating cashflow as a percentage of the outlay. None ONLY where there was no outlay to recover, which is the single legitimate null on this model.
capital_recovery_pct.title: Capital Recovery Pct

every_operating_year_non_positive.description: True means no year turns cash-positive, which is why project IRR is refused.
every_operating_year_non_positive.title: Every Operating Year Non Positive

lifetime_net_cashflow_gbp.description: Sum of the whole series, outlay included. Undiscounted bottom line.
lifetime_net_cashflow_gbp.title: Lifetime Net Cashflow Gbp

narrative.description: One reader-facing sentence carrying the measured position and its direction. Reaches rendered packs, so it holds no em/en dash (house style is zero).
narrative.title: Narrative

operating_cashflow_gbp.description: Sum of years 1..N: the cash the asset generates over the horizon.
operating_cashflow_gbp.title: Operating Cashflow Gbp

CapitalRecoveryAccount.title: CapitalRecoveryAccount

CashflowCase.description: The cash-flow series a lender sizes the debt on and tests the covenant against.
CashflowCase.title: CashflowCase

CashflowLineBasis.description: The money each cashflow line is stated in (D129): every line says real or nominal.
CashflowLineBasis.title: CashflowLineBasis

CmAuctionType.description: The Capacity Market auction an agreement was won in (SI 2014/2043 Sch 1 para 3).
CmAuctionType.title: CmAuctionType

ConfidenceBand.description:
How much weight a validation result can carry. Ordered worst to best.

Evidential strength — never a probability, never P50/P90, never a hurdle
(`docs/validation_requirements.md` §2). Defined here rather than in `gridq.quotes.confidence`
so the band and the Gate-2 ceiling can be **persisted on the QuoteRecord** and enforced by the
lifecycle gate (N21); `gridq.quotes.confidence` re-exports it, so its public name is unchanged.
ConfidenceBand.title: ConfidenceBand

ConnectionAgreementRef.description: The IC-1 agreement the restrictions apply under, by content hash.
ConnectionAgreementRef.title: ConnectionAgreementRef

ConstraintLibraryRef.description: Which constraint library, at which version and source hash, the result was solved with.
ConstraintLibraryRef.title: ConstraintLibraryRef

ConstructionPhase.description:
The construction programme: its length, the dated capex draws and the construction rate.

The drawdown profile is REQUIRED and has no default shape: a uniform or S-curve profile would
be an invented programme. ``idc_rate_pct`` may be omitted; the run then uses the supplied debt
terms' rate with a labelled warning, or excludes IDC with a warning when there is none
(D130, R4).

construction_months.description: Length of the build, in whole months.
construction_months.title: Construction Months

idc_rate_pct.description: Construction-facility interest rate, percent per year.
idc_rate_pct.title: Idc Rate Pct

ConstructionPhase.title: ConstructionPhase

ConstructionRecord.description: What the run did about construction, IDC and the COD delay (D130).
ConstructionRecord.title: ConstructionRecord

CovenantStatus.description:
DSCR covenant check (on the P90 case unless the lender terms name another).

``covenant`` is the default (event-of-default) threshold. The additive fields (WP-UW-03, D76;
the tiers half of H-05) carry what one key could not: ``source`` says whether the thresholds
came from the supplied lender terms or the assumption library; ``lock_up_dscr`` /
``lock_up_passes`` are the distribution lock-up tier; ``not_evaluated_reason`` says why
``passes`` is ``None``. All are derived from inputs the quote identity already pins, so
excluded from its hash (D78).
CovenantStatus.title: CovenantStatus

CustomerBill.description:
Annual customer bill decomposition, before vs after the solved dispatch.

In the **before-only** mode (no dispatch — see the module docstring) every AFTER-side field is
``None`` and only the BEFORE side and the battery-invariant fixed lines carry figures.

annual_saving_gbp.description: before − after; negative is representable (losses cost real money). ``None`` in the before-only mode — with no dispatch there is no saving, and 0.0 would read as a computed one.
annual_saving_gbp.title: Annual Saving Gbp

basis.description: What the bill includes AND excludes — the honesty label the proposal must carry alongside the headline.
basis.title: Basis

CustomerBill.title: CustomerBill

DataTier.description: Data quality tier of a site's load information.
DataTier.title: DataTier

DebtAssumptions.description:
Per-site debt assumptions (placeholder in v1; portfolio finance is Sim's).

**Percent, not fraction.** Every ``*_pct`` field here is a percentage: 60% gearing is
``60.0``, not ``0.6``. The distinction is enforced below because the ``[0, 100]`` bound alone
cannot catch it — ``0.6`` is a perfectly valid 0.6%, so a fraction written by mistake sails
through validation and sizes the debt **100× too small**, silently taking the DSCR, the
covenant verdict and the equity IRR with it (hostile review F-52).
DebtAssumptions.title: DebtAssumptions

Decommissioning.description: The decommissioning / site-restoration obligation (from the host-site agreement).

net_of_salvage.description: True when cost_gbp is already net of salvage.
net_of_salvage.title: Net Of Salvage

year.description: Operating year the cost falls in (1-based), or 'horizon_end'.
year.title: Year

Decommissioning.title: Decommissioning

DispatchProfile.description:
A representative dispatch day sliced from the solved schedule — the chart's data source.

``points`` is one day of half-hourly dispatch in period order; the day is selected
**deterministically** from the metered horizon (the highest-total-discharge day, earliest index
on ties — the most legible day of the dispatch strategy), recorded in ``selection_basis`` and
``representative_day_index`` so the reader knows which real day this is. Every value is a
real solved half-hour — **not** an average over days. ``interval_hours`` is the half-hourly Δt
(0.5). ``power_kw`` / ``energy_kwh`` / ``duration_hours`` echo the dispatched spec.
DispatchProfile.title: DispatchProfile

DispatchProfilePoint.description:
One half-hour of the representative dispatch day — real solved values, never invented.

``charge_kw`` / ``discharge_kw`` are the AC-side battery power in that half-hour (kW, both
``≥ 0``); ``soe_kwh`` is the state of energy (kWh); ``site_load_kw`` the metered site load;
``duos_rate_gbp_per_kwh`` the DUoS rate the dispatch faced; ``red_band`` whether the half-hour
sits in a DUoS red band; ``energy_price_gbp_per_kwh`` the time-of-use energy price the MILP
arbitraged (``None`` when the tariff had no time-mappable spread — not coerced to 0).
DispatchProfilePoint.title: DispatchProfilePoint

DrawdownPoint.description: One capex draw: a fraction of the capex spent a whole number of months before COD.

months_before_cod.description: Months before planned COD; 0 = at COD.
months_before_cod.title: Months Before Cod

DrawdownPoint.title: DrawdownPoint

DscrCovenantTerms.description:
The DSCR thresholds a lender tests (H-05: one key could not express the tiers).

``default_dscr`` is the event-of-default threshold; ``lock_up_dscr`` the distribution lock-up,
which sits at or above it. Either may be stated alone, but at least one must be: an empty
covenant block is not a covenant, and the record would claim a test that was never set.
DscrCovenantTerms.title: DscrCovenantTerms

DscrStatus.description: Why the DSCR on a record is, or is not, a number. Persisted on `DscrSummary.status`.
DscrStatus.title: DscrStatus

DscrSummary.description:
Debt Service Coverage Ratio summary (computed on the P90 case unless lender terms say not).

``status`` / ``unavailable_reason`` / ``cashflow_case`` are additive (WP-UW-03, D75). Every run
the model produces sets ``status``, and sets ``unavailable_reason`` whenever ``min_dscr`` is
``None``, so a missing ratio always carries its cause on the record instead of reading as
silence. They are ``None`` only on records written before D75. They are derived from inputs the
quote identity already pins, so they are excluded from the canonical hash input (D78).
DscrSummary.title: DscrSummary

EvidenceLink.description:
One IC-4 evidence object, by hash, and what it supports on the record that carries it.

``supports`` names the thing evidenced: a chassis field path (``connection.mic_kw``), a
revenue stream id, or a registered extension id. The reference says a document exists and
which one; whether it is valid, third-party and in scope is decided where the object is in
hand (`gridq.contracts.evidence.resolve_ref`, `assess`), never here.
EvidenceLink.title: EvidenceLink

EvidenceRef.description: A reference to an IC-4 instance by its content hash (what IC-1 and others embed).
EvidenceRef.title: EvidenceRef

FinancialCase.description:
The bankable result. Cashflows may be negative (year-0 capex) — a documented
exception to the no-negative-GBP rule.

capital_recovery.description: MANDATORY (D47): the always-defined return account. Deliberately has no default, so a FinancialCase cannot be constructed whose only return figure is a null IRR.

equity_irr.description: Levered (equity) IRR on the P50 base case (%); the P90 case governs the DSCR covenant. None when there is no debt or the equity series is non-conventional.
equity_irr.title: Equity Irr

lender_terms.description: WP-UW-03 (D75), additive: the lender terms the DSCR was sized and measured against, as supplied. None when the run had none (then dscr_summary.status says why there is no DSCR). A real input, so it enters the quote hash when set (D78).

lifecycle.description: WP-UW-17, additive and derived: what the run did with the lifecycle inputs and the library CPI key (indexation basis per line, construction / IDC / return basis, and the terminal, decommissioning and replacement ledger). Populated on every production run; None on historical records. Excluded from the quote hash (D132).

lifecycle_inputs.description: WP-UW-17, additive: the lifecycle inputs as supplied (construction programme, COD delay to stress, CM agreement indexation facts, terminal / decommissioning / replacement flows). None when the run had none. A real input, so it enters the quote hash when set (pop-if-None, D78).

p50_cashflows.description: Annual cashflows (GBP); year 0 is typically negative.
p50_cashflows.title: P50 Cashflows

p90_cashflows.description: Annual cashflows (GBP); year 0 is typically negative.
p90_cashflows.title: P90 Cashflows

FinancialCase.title: FinancialCase

Firmness.description: How firm a value stream is in the priced case.
Firmness.title: Firmness

HalfHourlyBasis.description:
How the half-hourly series underwriting priced was obtained (validation Gate 2).

Lives in the schema layer, not in `gridq.ingestion.hh_mandate` where the gate is, because the
basis has to be **persisted on the QuoteRecord** and read by downstream gates (N21). Before
that it existed only as a word interpolated into a warning string, so no gate could branch on
it: a modelled-basis run and a metered run were treated identically by every downstream check.
`gridq.ingestion.hh_mandate` re-exports this name, so the gate's own vocabulary is unchanged.
HalfHourlyBasis.title: HalfHourlyBasis

ImplementationLevel.description: How real the optimiser that produced a result is.
ImplementationLevel.title: ImplementationLevel

IndexationRecord.description: What the run did with `financing.cpi_pct_per_year` and the CM indexation rule.
IndexationRecord.title: IndexationRecord

LenderTerms.description:
A lender's debt terms for one site, as stated. Every figure is required: none is defaulted.

See the module docstring. ``gearing_pct`` is the maximum debt as a percentage of capex; with a
sculpted profile and a ``sculpting_target_dscr`` the debt is the smaller of that cap and what
the case CFADS supports at the target (D77).

covenant.description: Default and lock-up DSCR thresholds. None when the terms state no covenant.

gearing_pct.description: Maximum debt as a percentage of capex, percent.
gearing_pct.title: Gearing Pct

sculpting_target_dscr.description: Flat DSCR the sculpted service is sized to. Sculpted amortisation only.
sculpting_target_dscr.title: Sculpting Target Dscr

LenderTerms.title: LenderTerms

LenderTermsProvenance.description: Who stated these terms, and on what. Travels with the terms onto the record.

as_of.description: Date the terms were stated, if known.
as_of.title: As Of

evidence_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the source document, when one is held.
evidence_sha256.title: Evidence Sha256

reference.description: Term-sheet id, lender and date, or for synthetic terms what they are for.
reference.title: Reference

LenderTermsProvenance.title: LenderTermsProvenance

LenderTermsSource.description: Where the lender terms came from. Only a term sheet can support a bankable verdict.
LenderTermsSource.title: LenderTermsSource

LifecycleFlowEntry.description: One row of the lifecycle capital-flow ledger (D131).
LifecycleFlowEntry.title: LifecycleFlowEntry

LifecycleInputs.description:
The lifecycle facts for one site, as stated. Every block is optional and independent; none
is defaulted. See the module docstring.

``cod_delay_months`` is the delay to STRESS in the scenario table (a zero-weight ``cod_delay``
row), not a delay applied to the base case. ``replacements=()`` is a declared "no replacement",
which is modelled; ``None`` is "not stated", which is excluded and asked for.
LifecycleInputs.title: LifecycleInputs

LifecycleProvenance.description: Who stated the lifecycle facts, and on what. Travels with the inputs onto the record.

as_of.description: Date the facts were stated, if known.
as_of.title: As Of

evidence_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the source document, when one is held.
evidence_sha256.title: Evidence Sha256

reference.description: Programme / quotation / agreement id and date, or what synthetic inputs are for.
reference.title: Reference

LifecycleProvenance.title: LifecycleProvenance

LifecycleRecord.description: The derived lifecycle record on every `FinancialCase` (WP-UW-17).
LifecycleRecord.title: LifecycleRecord

LifecycleSource.description: Where the lifecycle facts came from.
LifecycleSource.title: LifecycleSource

LineBasisEntry.description: One cashflow line and its basis.
LineBasisEntry.title: LineBasisEntry

MarketStream.description: The value-stream registry (the vocabulary of revenue/cost streams).
MarketStream.title: MarketStream

OptimisationResult.description: The object the engine returns. Frozen shared contract (with the stream registry).
OptimisationResult.title: OptimisationResult

PriceBasis.description:
The money a user-stated £ is expressed in (D131, R2).

``real_at_as_of`` is money of the ``as_of`` date, which the model takes to be its year-1 price
base (the base every library £ is stated on): on a CPI-indexed run it escalates by
``(1 + c)^(t − 1)`` in operating year ``t``, and no escalation is applied between ``as_of`` and
COD (a delay included). ``nominal_as_entered`` is the money of the year the flow falls in and
is never escalated.
PriceBasis.title: PriceBasis

PriceRecommendation.description:
The recommended price/structure that hits the target return.

``counterfactual_import_gbp_per_kwh`` (additive, 2026-07-07) is the customer's current
blended import energy cost (mean of the tariff's import rates plus £/kWh levy lines — a
disclosed blended-rate approximation, the same convention the parasitic-load cost line
uses). ``exceeds_counterfactual`` is True when the price required to hit the target return
is ABOVE what the customer already pays per kWh — i.e. the project is not commercially
viable as a fixed PPA and the number must never be presented as an offer. ``None`` on
historical records and where either side is unavailable.

equity_closed_loop_gbp_per_kwh.title: Equity Closed Loop Gbp Per Kwh

PriceRecommendation.title: PriceRecommendation

PriceStructure.description: Commercial structure of the price recommendation.
PriceStructure.title: PriceStructure

year.description: Operating year the replacement falls in (1-based).
year.title: Year

ReplacementComponent.description:
What is replaced. Battery modules are NOT a component here: replacing cells is
augmentation, and the model sizes the asset on day one for end-of-life capability.
ReplacementComponent.title: ReplacementComponent

ReturnBasis.description: The timeline the headline IRRs were measured on.
ReturnBasis.title: ReturnBasis

ScenarioSensitivity.description:
One scenario's DSCR/return outcome — a row of the Output-2 sensitivity table.

Produced by re-running the financial model under a scenario (Low/Central/High). ``min_dscr``
and ``irr_pct`` are ``None`` when their inputs are unavailable (e.g. no debt → no DSCR) — never
guessed.
ScenarioSensitivity.title: ScenarioSensitivity

SelectionStatus.description:
What the sizing selection concluded (distinct from the solver's numerical status).

A dispatch can solve OPTIMAL at every candidate size and the run can still end with no
recommendable system: when no candidate produces any return metric (project IRR or levered
return), the honest verdict is ``no_viable_configuration`` — a first-class economics verdict,
never a smallest-grid-corner "recommendation" (the pre-2026-07-07 failure mode). Additive and
optional on `OptimisationResult` so historical records (``None``) still load.
SelectionStatus.title: SelectionStatus

SizingGrid.description:
The full evaluated sizing grid + the chosen optimum — the 3D surface's data source.

``points`` is every evaluated candidate in deterministic ``(power, duration)`` order (inherited
from `SearchSpace.candidates()`); ``selected`` is the chosen optimum — the covenant-feasible
best, the unlevered best, the indicatively-chosen fallback, or ``None`` when none exists, which
is honest, not an error. ``selection_basis`` names which of the four it is (they are enumerated
on the field itself below), and must be read alongside it:
the grid used to report ``selected=None`` and "no bankable candidate" on runs whose
`OptimisationResult` said ``selection_status=SELECTED`` and named a kW, with both persisted on
the same `QuoteRecord` (N16). ``covenant`` is the P90-DSCR covenant the feasibility flag is
measured against (``None`` when unknown). ``bankable`` mirrors `SizingRun.bankable` — never
``True`` on the placeholder.
SizingGrid.title: SizingGrid

SizingGridPoint.description:
One evaluated (power, duration) candidate and the scalars the surface/objective read.

Mirrors `gridq.sizing.sizer.CandidateEvaluation`, keeping only the plottable, serializable
scalars (the heavy per-candidate `OptimisationResult`/`FinancialModelResult` are dropped).
``levered_return_pct`` is the equity IRR (P50 basis; ``None`` without injected debt — the
surface's z-axis), ``project_irr_pct`` the unlevered fallback. ``passes_covenant`` is the
P90-DSCR feasibility flag — ``True``/``False`` when the DSCR is available, ``None`` when it is
not (no debt structure), never coerced to ``False``; ``min_p90_dscr`` is likewise ``None`` when
unavailable.

**The revenue fields (``0.2.0``) exist because their absence made the record say something
false.** Up to 2026-08-17 a point carried every ratio the objective ranks on and not one £, so
a run that selected nothing persisted an evaluated grid that could not state what any candidate
had *earned*. The pack then read as "this site earns nothing" on sites whose own recorded
verdict said the dispatch had discharged tens of MWh: the true sentence is "the best candidate
earns £X/yr and still does not cover its costs", and only the second is a result rather than an
implication. Both are negatives; only the second is evidenced. (It also makes an existing claim
true: `optimisation.valuation` already tells readers "the per-candidate figures are in the
sizing grid".)

Read the £ fields by these rules:

* ``annual_revenue_gbp`` is the **priced floor** — firm + contracted streams only, copied from
  ``CashflowModel.total_annual_revenue_gbp``, the identical figure the finance model built this
  candidate's cashflows on. It is NOT the sum of ``revenue_streams``, which also carries the
  held-out entries.
* ``None`` on any £ field means **no cashflow model was built for this candidate** (see
  ``priceable``) — genuinely unmeasured, never a zero. A ``0.0`` means measured and zero.
* The costs are the two recorded lines EBITDA nets off, kept separate exactly as
  `CashflowModel` keeps them, so "does not cover its costs" can be checked rather than
  asserted. Neither is escalated and neither includes capex (year-1 basis, as elsewhere).
SizingGridPoint.title: SizingGridPoint

SizingGridStreamRevenue.description:
One value stream's year-1 revenue for one evaluated candidate, with its floor membership.

A copy of the four fields of the candidate's own `ValueStreamResult` that a reader needs to
tell one ``£0.00`` from another, and nothing else (the per-stream warning prose — a 250-word
paragraph repeated across every stream of a no-spec run — stays on the top-level record where
it is stated once).

**Why `in_priced_floor` is stored rather than left to be re-derived.** A recorded zero has
three different meanings and they must not collapse (D45):

* ``in_priced_floor=True`` with ``annual_revenue_gbp == 0.0`` — the stream IS in the priced
  floor, the optimiser priced it, and the trade came out at nothing. A measured result.
* ``in_priced_floor=False`` — the stream was held OUT of the floor by its firmness/gate
  (``gate_status`` says which), so its £ is upside and its zero is not a floor measurement at
  all. A held-out stream may equally carry a **non-zero** ``annual_revenue_gbp``: conditional
  capacity-market upside does exactly that, and summing it into the floor would be a false
  claim in the opposite direction.
* The whole list empty, or `SizingGridPoint.annual_revenue_gbp` ``None`` — nothing was
  measured for this candidate. Never written as ``0.0``.

It is stamped from `schemas.market.is_priced_floor`, the same predicate
`finance.cashflows.revenue_by_stream` filters on, so the floor breakdown here and the floor
total in `SizingGridPoint.annual_revenue_gbp` cannot disagree about which streams compose it.
SizingGridStreamRevenue.title: SizingGridStreamRevenue

SolverMetadata.description: Run metadata stamped onto a result (versions, seed, timing, environment).
SolverMetadata.title: SolverMetadata

StatusHistoryEntry.description: One prior lifecycle state, for the append-only history trail.

TerminalValue.description: The residual value at the horizon, received in the final operating year.

TerminalValueBasis.description:
How the residual value at the horizon is stated. No perpetuity: it would invent a growth
rate for a finite asset sized for its end of life (D131).

Additive and optional — carried through from the gate; it never affects the firmness bar (a gated-upside stream still cannot be FIRM) and drives the proposal's 'consent given' line.
